researchIntro: These are examples of topics available to undergraduate researchers. Use them as starting points for the questions you want to explore.

research.label: SMALL TRANSFORMERS
research.title: Small Transformers
research.description: Explore lightweight models for the actions and dialogue of game characters. Learn from play logs to estimate difficulty and reasons for player dropout, informing game balance and player experience.

research.label: DATA-CONSCIOUS GENERATION
research.title: Image generation with limited data
research.description: Investigate high-quality image generation using medium-sized datasets with verified rights and provenance, alongside synthesized data, without relying on unauthorized data collection.

research.label: WORLD MODELS
research.title: World models & interactive AI
research.description: Use approaches such as latent diffusion to predict changes in the world from video, images, and action sequences. Develop predictive and world-understanding models for games and interactive AI.

computeText: We use public supercomputers such as ABCI 3.0 at AIST and TSUBAME 4.0 at Institute of Science Tokyo. Our research connects distributed training with implementation in interactive systems.
projectsIntro: Examples connecting AI, games, and interaction. These previous projects offer starting points for new research questions.

projects.name: Kinetics
projects.label: INTERACTION
projects.title: A gamepad controlled by finger tilting
projects.description: A mathematical model for an on-screen gamepad controlled by tilting a finger, exploring new possibilities for touch interaction.

projects.name: Cymotion
projects.label: CHARACTER ANIMATION
projects.title: Characters that respond to their surroundings
projects.description: A next-generation animation system that retrieves and blends motion clips based on context, such as terrain and NPCs, to automatically select suitable character actions.

projects.name: Learned PRNG
projects.label: GENERATIVE MODELS
projects.title: Learning to generate random numbers
projects.description: Train a generator from existing random numbers using WGAN-GP to produce outputs that pass the NIST test suite. Explore learned random number generation alongside manually designed algorithms.

projects.name: Sketch2Map
projects.label: CREATIVITY SUPPORT
projects.title: From a hand-drawn sketch to a game map
projects.description: A two-stage pix2pix conditional GAN system that turns hand-drawn sketches into game maps. The work is also featured in the book Deep Learning in Gaming and Animations as an application of deep learning to games.

projects.name: Rayauth
projects.label: VISION & AUTHENTICATION
projects.title: Authenticating cards through changing light
projects.description: Learn spatiotemporal changes in light caused by holograms and transparent ink structures on cards. Use a smartphone camera to distinguish genuine cards, counterfeits, and screen displays, exploring authentication without embedded chips.
